questions.q: What does Moore's law describe, according to the summary?
a: Computing power doubling roughly every twelve months
The cost of software falling every two years
Internet speeds tripling with each new generation
The number of technology users doubling annually
questions.why: Moore noticed that twice as many transistors could fit on a chip of the same size.

questions.q: What point does the smartphone comparison with a 1970 supercomputer make?
a: Powerful technology is now cheap and widely available
Phones have replaced every other kind of computer
Supercomputers remain necessary for innovation
Technology has stopped becoming more affordable
questions.why: The phone is far cheaper and far more powerful, showing how far exponential growth has come.

questions.q: Which two technologies does the summary identify as huge opportunities?
a: Artificial intelligence and sensors
Robotics and drones
Biotechnology and 3D printing
Solar power and batteries
questions.why: The summary says these areas can scale exponentially and will have enormous impact.

questions.q: What are the three features of a skunk works operation?
a: One clear goal, no bureaucracy, and an isolated team
A large budget, many managers, and public fanfare
A flexible goal, strict oversight, and open offices
A secret goal, outside investors, and remote workers
questions.why: The original Skunk Works built a jet fighter in 143 days with these conditions.

questions.q: Why does the summary recommend creating a skunk works for your idea?
a: To learn quickly whether it works instead of dabbling for years
To attract investors before building a prototype
To avoid sharing credit with your employer
To qualify for government research funding
questions.why: A focused burst of work reveals whether an idea holds up in the real world.
